classification.difficultyReason: Apply a snow-to-rain equivalence to a larger snowfall, retaining an exact fractional result.

content.prompt: 160 mm of snow contains as much water as 15 mm of rain. A town within the Arctic Circle receives about 4250 mm of snow a year. If the snow had fallen as rain, what would the equivalent rainfall for the year have been?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Rain equivalent of 1 mm of snow}&=\frac{15}{160}\text{ mm}\\\text{Rain equivalent of 4250 mm of snow}&=4250\times\frac{15}{160}\text{ mm}\\\text{Rain equivalent of 4250 mm of snow}&=\frac{6375}{16}\text{ mm}\\\text{Rain equivalent of 4250 mm of snow}&=398\frac{7}{16}\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$
